atoms.span: Labor Notes is an American media and organizing project
founded in 1979 by labor activist Kim Moody
it reports on rank-and-file union democracy, strikes, and independent worker-led organizing efforts.
Publishes 11 issues annually covering shop-floor strategy, union elections, and grassroots campaigns across major sectors.
Operating as a voice for the "troublemaking wing" of the labor movement

mt: 'LABOR NOTES' IN AI MODE — THE PROJECT AT ITS GRAIN, ITS SUPPORT FOR REFORM CAUCUSES AND TDU GIVEN; ITS INDEPENDENCE TO PRINT CRITICISM OF LEADERS NOT CARRIED
d: THE PROJECT, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31, AI MODE: 'Labor Notes is an American media and organizing project founded in 1979 by labor activist Kim Moody.' Fact table (1979, Kim Moody, Detroit); core initiatives: the magazine, the biennial conference, workshops, movement building ('historically supporting factions like the Teamsters for a Democratic Union (TDU)').
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the project, AI Mode gives its founding, its headquarters and its four lines of work, and offers more.
findings: THE CAUCUSES CARRIED. 'Bridges isolated reform caucuses to help democratize major organizations, historically supporting factions like the Teamsters for a Democratic Union (TDU).' #1725 counts TDU among the structures that held critique inside a union by building a constituency able to replace officials.

THE INDEPENDENCE NOT CARRIED. 'And as an independent publication, we’re free to include the voices who say we could be doing better—and tell how.' and 'For the most part, our leaders are doing a poor job of navigating us through the crisis.' (the project's About page). The organ that prints criticism of union leadership is the condition #1725 names; the composition gives the magazine's subjects and not its standing.
analysis: Faithful, and close to #1725 where it names the caucuses Labor Notes supports. The project's own statement of why it can carry that criticism, its independence as a publication, is absent.
per_note: The founder named; the project's site and Wikipedia among the cards.
